lesson_title: Algebraic Language: Variables, Terms and Coefficients
hook_text: Three apples plus five bananas is not eight anything.
clip_script:
Here is algebra as a shopping basket. You put three apples, five bananas and one loaf of bread in a basket. Written as an expression: three a plus five b plus one l, or three a plus five b plus l. Each kind of item is a term. The letter is the kind of item — the variable, because the price of an apple could be anything until you reach the till. The number in front is how many of that item — the coefficient. The loaf has coefficient one, which you do not bother to write.

Like terms are the same kind of item. If a friend adds two more apples to the basket, you now have three a plus two a, which is five a. You can add apples to apples. You cannot add apples to bananas: three a plus five b is just three a plus five b, two kinds of item, two terms, and no amount of wishing turns it into eight of anything.
visual_style: A basket filling with apples, bananas and a loaf; the expression 3a + 5b + l assembling above it; two more apples dropping in and 3a + 2a merging to 5a while 5b stays put
